payload.claim: `History.model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)` turns on strict mode for the whole model, where every other departure from lax validation in this file is a field-level `Field(..., strict=True)` carrying its own measured-reason comment (`estimated_lines` at :214, 'Strict, since a lax `int` read `true` as 1 (measured 2026-09-22)'; `estimate_measured` at :216). `History` is the only model in `saffron/` with a model-level `strict=True` (checked: `Mutant`, `Criterion`, `Spec`, every model in `review.py`, `policy.py` and `spec_review.py` use bare `ConfigDict(extra="forbid")`), and no comment says why `batches` needs it or why `command` is swept in too. CLAUDE.md: 'A measured fact beats a reasoned one, and the comment says which' — this field-less, uncommented strict setting breaks that pattern even though the tests show the behaviour it buys (refusing `'yes'` and `1` for `batches`) is intentional.
